title: Spend now. A Day is coming with no deals and no connections.
subtitle: The window to give closes

picture.label: What will not work on that Day

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells believers to {reward}rush to spend in this life{/reward}, before a Day when no one can {trap}ransom himself even with the earth's fill of gold{/trap}, and friendship and relations will not help. He links it to 23:101: no kinship that Day.
now: You know a guy who can get you in anywhere. Your cousin sorts every problem. Your card has a high limit. {trap}None of that works on that Day.{/trap} What you gave from it today does.
old: I will give generously once I have more saved up.
new: Today is the only time giving still counts; on that Day nothing can be bought.
try: Give something today from this month's money, not from some future surplus.

title: The Ever-Living who never sleeps holds everything, without tiring.
subtitle: Ayat al-Kursi, the greatest verse
then: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy bin Ka'b which verse was greatest. He said Ayat al-Kursi, and the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}congratulations on your knowledge{/reward}. In Abu Hurayrah's story, even Shaytan admitted that reciting it at bedtime brings {idea}a guard from Allah until morning{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said: he told the truth, though he is a liar.
now: Lying in bed replaying the bills, the kids, the scan results. You feel like you have to stay awake to hold it together. {idea}You do not.{/idea} The One who holds the heavens and earth does not get tired, and He does not sleep.
old: If I stop worrying, everything will fall apart.
new: The One who never sleeps is holding everything, so I can rest.
try: Recite Ayat al-Kursi tonight before sleeping, slowly, thinking about each line.

title: Faith cannot be forced. Hold the handhold that never breaks.
subtitle: Truth is clear enough to stand without pressure
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}do not force anyone into Islam, for its proofs are plain and clear{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said the verse came about Ansar children raised among a Jewish tribe; when that tribe left, the parents wanted to keep them. Abdullah bin Salam dreamed of {reward}climbing a pillar and grasping a handle{/reward}; the Prophet ﷺ said: that is the firmest handhold.
now: You want your teenager to pray, your friend to come back to faith. You nag, guilt, push. {idea}Faith cannot be installed from outside.{/idea} Show it clearly, live it well, and let them reach for the handle themselves.
old: If I push hard enough, I can make someone believe.
new: Truth is clear enough on its own; my job is to show it, and hold tight myself.
try: Replace one nagging reminder to someone with a kind example of what you hope for them.

title: Allah brings you from many darknesses into one light.
subtitle: Truth is one, falsehood comes in many forms
then: Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}light is singular and darkness plural{/idea}, because truth is one while falsehood has many branches. He cites 6:153: follow My straight path, {trap}not other paths that scatter you{/trap}. Allah takes believers out of the darkness of doubt and hesitation.
now: Doubt at 2am. Anxiety about the future. Envy watching other people's lives online. {trap}Each darkness feels different.{/trap} The way out is the same one light, and Allah is the one who leads you there.
old: I have too many problems to know where to start.
new: My darknesses are many, but the way out is one, and Allah is my guide to it.
try: Name one darkness you are in right now and ask Allah, as your Wali, to bring you out.

title: Power made him argue with God. The sunrise left him speechless.
subtitle: When authority goes to your head

row.title: bring the sun from the west

then: Mujahid said the king was Nimrod. Ibn Kathir says {trap}his long rule made him tyrannical{/trap} until he claimed to give life and death himself. Ibrahim answered with the sun: {idea}Allah brings it from the east, so bring it from the west{/idea}. The king was left with nothing to say.
now: The promotion that makes you short with the junior staff. The admin rights in the group chat. Being the eldest who always decides. {trap}A little power makes it easy to forget who gave it.{/trap}
old: Because I am in charge, my view is the one that counts.
new: Any authority I have is on loan from the One who moves the sun.
try: Watch the sunrise or sunset today and remember who controls it.

title: He doubted the ruin could live. He woke a century later.
subtitle: Allah shows you, slowly, that He can restore
then: Ali and Ibn Abbas said this was Uzayr. He passed a ruined town and wondered {trap}how Allah could ever revive it{/trap}. Allah let him die for a century; he woke thinking it was part of a day. His figs and juice had not spoiled, and he watched {reward}his donkey's bones gathered and covered in flesh{/reward}.
now: Your marriage feels like a ruin. Your faith feels empty. Your hometown or your health has collapsed. {trap}You stand there thinking, how could this ever come back?{/trap} Allah restores things that look fully dead.
old: Some things are too broken to ever be restored.
new: If Allah can raise a hundred-year-old ruin, He can restore what I think is lost.
try: Make dua today for one thing in your life you had given up as too broken.

title: Ibrahim believed, and still asked to see so his heart could rest.
subtitle: Wanting certainty is not the same as doubt
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}we are more liable to seek certainty than Ibrahim{/idea}. Allah had him call four birds back from the hills, and they came rushing. Ibn Abbas called this {reward}the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an{/reward}, because Allah accepted Ibrahim's simple yes, and it speaks to the doubts Shaytan whispers into hearts.
now: You pray, you fast, you believe. And sometimes a question still gnaws at you at night. {reward}That does not make you a hypocrite.{/reward} Even Ibrahim asked to see. Bring the question to Allah, not away from Him.
old: If I have questions about my faith, I must not really believe.
new: I can believe and still ask Allah to settle my heart, as Ibrahim did.
try: Take one question you have been afraid to ask about faith and ask someone you trust.
